title: Whose Cells Are in a Seed?

scenes.visual: Title card 'Whose Cells Are in a Seed?' over a maize ear cartoon. COLOUR MAP (both films): maternal chromosome sets = MAGENTA blocks, paternal sets = TEAL blocks; each set is one rounded rectangle block, stacked in a short column beside the cell or tissue it belongs to. Tissue fills: embryo GREEN, endosperm CREAM, seed coat BROWN, fruit wall ORANGE, pollen and tube PALE YELLOW. Plant drawings are flat cartoons labelled 'schematic'. All numbers appear only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: Break open a maize kernel. Part of it is a baby plant, part is its food, and part is a wrapper. Which parts came from the father?
scenes.visual: A single maize kernel splits open in cross-section (schematic). Three regions light up in turn: a small GREEN embryo at one side, a big CREAM food block, a thin BROWN-ORANGE outer skin. A question mark hovers over each, then a label 'father?'.
scenes.narration: Break open a maize kernel. Part of it is a baby plant, part is its food, and part is a wrapper. Which parts came from the father?

scenes.tts: We can answer by counting chromosome sets. One set is the chromosomes of one egg or one sperm. The mother's sets will be magenta blocks. The father's will be teal.
scenes.visual: A cartoon egg drops one MAGENTA block into a tray labelled 'one maternal set'; a cartoon sperm drops one TEAL block labelled 'one paternal set'. Legend appears top right and stays for the whole film.
scenes.narration: We can answer by counting chromosome sets. One set is the chromosomes of one egg or one sperm. The mother's sets will be magenta blocks. The father's will be teal.

scenes.tts: Start with the father. A pollen grain is not a sperm. It is a tiny separate generation of the plant, two or three cells, and it makes two sperm.
scenes.visual: Zoom from a maize tassel into an anther; a PALE YELLOW pollen grain fills the screen, showing a large tube cell with a small cell inside that splits into two small sperm. Each cell gets one TEAL block beside it. Label 'male gametophyte: 2 or 3 cells'.
scenes.narration: Start with the father. A pollen grain is not a sperm. It is a tiny separate generation of the plant, two or three cells, and it makes two sperm.

scenes.tts: Every cell in the grain carries one set from the father. The grain lands on a stigma, the sticky tip that catches pollen. It grows a tube down to an ovule, and the two sperm ride inside.
scenes.visual: The grain lands on a hairy maize silk labelled 'stigma'. A PALE YELLOW tube snakes down the silk toward a small oval labelled 'ovule'; two TEAL-tagged sperm travel inside the tube tip.
scenes.narration: Every cell in the grain carries one set from the father. The grain lands on a stigma, the sticky tip that catches pollen. It grows a tube down to an ovule, and the two sperm ride inside.

scenes.tts: Inside the ovule waits the mother's tiny generation, the embryo sac. It comes from one spore, so its nuclei are all copies of one maternal set.
scenes.visual: Cut into the ovule: a pale embryo sac outline appears inside BROWN-outlined layers. One MAGENTA block appears, then copies itself several times into the sac's nuclei, label 'all copies of one maternal set'.
scenes.narration: Inside the ovule waits the mother's tiny generation, the embryo sac. It comes from one spore, so its nuclei are all copies of one maternal set.

scenes.tts: Three kinds of cells matter. The egg holds one magenta block. The large central cell holds two identical copies of that same set. Two synergids sit beside the egg.
scenes.visual: Inside the sac three cell types are labelled: 'egg' with one MAGENTA block; a big 'central cell' with two identical MAGENTA blocks marked '=' between them; two small 'synergids' flanking the egg, glowing faintly.
scenes.narration: Three kinds of cells matter. The egg holds one magenta block. The large central cell holds two identical copies of that same set. Two synergids sit beside the egg.

scenes.tts: The synergids signal to the tube. The tube bursts into one of them and releases both sperm.
scenes.visual: Faint wavy signal lines spread from the synergids; the tube tip turns toward them, enters through a small gap in the BROWN layers, and bursts into one synergid. Two TEAL-tagged sperm pop out, one drifting toward the egg, one toward the central cell.
scenes.narration: The synergids signal to the tube. The tube bursts into one of them and releases both sperm.

scenes.tts: One sperm fuses with the egg. That makes the zygote, which grows into the embryo. Its stack is one magenta block and one teal.
scenes.visual: Sperm and egg merge into a cell labelled 'zygote'; it buds into a small GREEN 'embryo' cartoon. Beside it, a stack: one MAGENTA block under one TEAL block, label 'embryo: 1 + 1'.
scenes.narration: One sperm fuses with the egg. That makes the zygote, which grows into the embryo. Its stack is one magenta block and one teal.

scenes.tts: The other sperm fuses with the central cell. That cell already holds two copies of the mother's set. How many blocks will the new tissue carry? How many are the father's?
scenes.visual: The second sperm approaches the central cell's two MAGENTA blocks. Question card: 'How many blocks? How many TEAL?'
scenes.narration: The other sperm fuses with the central cell. That cell already holds two copies of the mother's set. How many blocks will the new tissue carry? How many are the father's?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds; 5-second ring timer bottom right.

scenes.tts: Three blocks, only one of them teal. This is the endosperm, the food store for the embryo: two maternal sets, one paternal.
scenes.visual: The sperm merges; the stack grows to two MAGENTA plus one TEAL. The cell fills with CREAM and swells into a big block labelled 'endosperm: 2 + 1', beside the GREEN embryo.
scenes.narration: Three blocks, only one of them teal. This is the endosperm, the food store for the embryo: two maternal sets, one paternal.

scenes.tts: One sperm starts the baby plant, and the other starts its food. This is double fertilization.
scenes.visual: Split screen: left 'sperm + egg → embryo (1 + 1)', right 'sperm + central cell → endosperm (2 + 1)'. Title across both: 'double fertilization'. Small footnote: 'most flowering plants'.
scenes.narration: One sperm starts the baby plant, and the other starts its food. This is double fertilization.

scenes.tts: Layers of the mother's own tissue surround the embryo sac. They become the seed coat, with no teal at all.
scenes.visual: The BROWN integument layers around the sac develop into a coat labelled 'seed coat' (drawn thin, as in maize). Its stack: two MAGENTA blocks, a dashed empty slot where TEAL would go, label 'seed coat: 2 + 0, the mother's tissue'.
scenes.narration: Layers of the mother's own tissue surround the embryo sac. They become the seed coat, with no teal at all.

scenes.tts: The ovary wall around the ovule becomes the fruit wall. It is the mother's tissue too. In maize, it is the kernel's thin outer skin.
scenes.visual: Zoom out: the ORANGE ovary wall around the seed becomes 'fruit wall', stack two MAGENTA + empty TEAL slot. The view snaps back to the maize kernel cross-section with the ORANGE skin labelled 'fruit wall (pericarp)'.
scenes.narration: The ovary wall around the ovule becomes the fruit wall. It is the mother's tissue too. In maize, it is the kernel's thin outer skin.

scenes.tts: One kernel, three ledgers. Embryo, one and one. Endosperm, two and one. Coat and fruit wall, two and none.
scenes.visual: The kernel from the opening, now colour-coded, with three block stacks pinned to it: GREEN embryo '1 + 1', CREAM endosperm '2 + 1', BROWN/ORANGE coat and fruit wall '2 + 0'.
scenes.narration: One kernel, three ledgers. Embryo, one and one. Endosperm, two and one. Coat and fruit wall, two and none.

scenes.tts: This count holds for most flowering plants. Water lilies, for one, change the numbers but keep the logic.
scenes.visual: A small water-lily cartoon appears; its endosperm stack shows one MAGENTA + one TEAL, label 'water lilies: 1 + 1'. The main maize ledger stays at centre, label 'most flowering plants'.
scenes.narration: This count holds for most flowering plants. Water lilies, for one, change the numbers but keep the logic.

scenes.tts: Pollen landing on a stigma is pollination. Fertilization comes later, inside the ovule, and only if a tube arrives.
scenes.visual: Timeline arrow: 'pollen lands on stigma = pollination' at left, a long gap with the tube growing, 'sperm fuse in ovule = fertilization' at right. A second grain lands but grows no tube; its timeline stops, label 'pollinated, never fertilized'.
scenes.narration: Pollen landing on a stigma is pollination. Fertilization comes later, inside the ovule, and only if a tube arrives.

scenes.tts: So the father sends one set, twice. His sets enter only the embryo and the endosperm. The seed coat and fruit wall are the mother's own tissue.
scenes.visual: Two TEAL arrows from the pollen grain point into the GREEN embryo and CREAM endosperm stacks; the BROWN coat and ORANGE fruit wall wrap around them, MAGENTA only. Label 'father: embryo and endosperm only; coat and fruit wall: mother'.
scenes.narration: So the father sends one set, twice. His sets enter only the embryo and the endosperm. The seed coat and fruit wall are the mother's own tissue.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex. One line: 'The father reaches embryo and endosperm; coat and fruit wall stay maternal.'
